summary: Instagram is doing the work: almost every Hindi video gets 1,000+ views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly gets under 60 views, with a few exceptions. The best videos use a surprising 'it doesn't see/hear the way you think' hook about a simple, familiar gadget or robot (gyro robot, clap switch, PIR sensor), and they earn the most likes, saves and shares. Weak videos are generic 'How does X work?' questions about public-place devices (lift, mall door, taps, smoke detector), which stay under 500 views and get almost no saves or shares. The one English video got no Instagram reach, so it is not yet a proven path.
winningPattern: A hands-on maker/robot or Arduino-style sensor subject (gyro robot, clap switch, PIR, line follower, mic, IR robot) with a Hindi 'myth-flip' hook: 'X doesn't do what you think, it only does Y' or a 'without this part, it fails' dramatic consequence. Short Hinglish titles with one emoji and #shorts, posted first and mainly to Instagram Reels, ideally as a series (clap switch got two strong videos). Posting daily in late Oct to early Nov also helped.
doMore: Open with a surprising reversal ('doesn't see, only feels/hears') or a failure demo ('without X, robot falls')
Choose robots and hobby modules students can build: gyro, clap switch, line follower, mic, IR obstacle sensor
Make follow-up series from winners, such as a clap switch part 3 or a gyro robot part 2
End with a save-worthy takeaway like a wiring tip or pin diagram to boost saves and shares
Test YouTube separately with the strongest hooks, and check why the IR robot video got 10 shares on Instagram but only 14 YouTube views
stopDoing: Generic 'Kaise kaam karta hai?' titles about public devices (lift, mall door, tap, smoke detector)
Posting several near-duplicate topics (IR sensor, smoke detector, tap) within days of each other
Publishing English versions until Hindi YouTube and Instagram are working consistently
